fields.meta_title: Course Landing Page Examples by Course Format | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See a course landing page for four formats: cohort seats, a free first lesson, a placement quiz, and team requests. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Course Landing Page Shaped Around How You Teach
fields.hero_description: Build a course landing page for a cohort, a self-paced course, or team training, with every enrollment in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What the Page Does Once a Student Clicks Enroll
fields.features_subheading: A course landing page sells one course to one kind of student. These six parts take a visitor from the headline to a saved enrollment.
fields.feature_1:
One prompt for the page and its tables

Tell Emergent the course format and what to ask each student. It builds the page with its enrollment form and the table behind it, then changes any part when you prompt again.
fields.feature_2:
Every enrollment is a row you own

Each enrollment saves the student's answers and chosen cohort to a database you own. Connect your email tool or CRM through its API, and the app syncs every new student there too.
fields.feature_3:
Seats left, counted as students enroll

Cap a cohort at the number you can teach. The app counts each enrollment as it saves and updates the seats left on the page in real time, for every visitor reading it at that moment.
fields.feature_4:
A placement quiz, one question per screen

Show a few questions before anyone enrolls, one per screen, then score the answers. The app sends each student to the class page for their level and saves the score on their row.
fields.feature_5:
Alerts for requests you answer in person

Pick the requests you want to handle yourself, such as a team asking for 10 or more seats. Each one that matches reaches you as an email, a Slack message, or an in-app alert.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain now, your repository later

Publish the course page on your own domain; custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, the full code exports to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.usecase_heading: One Course Page for Each Way You Teach
fields.tab_content_1:
6 of 30 seats left after Junie enrolls

Fernhollow Studio caps its 6-week watercolor cohort at 30 seats, and the course page shows how many are still open. The count drops the moment an enrollment saves. Junie Calloway enrolled as student 24, and every visitor on the page saw 6 of 30 seats left.
fields.tab_content_2:
Leave an email and lesson 1 plays

Brinemark Kitchen sells a self-paced sourdough course in 14 lessons and gives the first one away. A visitor types an email, and lesson 1 starts on the same page. The app adds each signup to the email tool the school connected, and 212 people signed up this week.
fields.tab_content_3:
Odile Marchetti places into Intermediate with a 4

Tidewell Spanish asks 6 questions before a new student picks a class, one per screen. A score of 3 or 4 of 6 points to Intermediate. Odile Marchetti scored 4 of 6, landed on the Intermediate class page, and enrolled with her score saved.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bram Okafor hears about every team of 10 or more

Quarry Lane Analytics sells its SQL course to companies as well as to individuals, and the course page asks how many seats a company needs. Any request for 10 or more seats emails instructor Bram Okafor. Halvorsen Freight asked for 18 seats, and Bram got the email.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Course Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a course landing page, build it with Emergent, and test every enrollment path before it goes live.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the change the course makes
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick the format before the layout
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write one sentence on who the course is for and what they can do at the end, such as paint a finished watercolor in 6 weeks. That sentence becomes your headline, and it tells you which visitors the page is not for.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide whether students start together in a cohort, start any time at their own pace, or join as a company. The format sets what the button asks for: a seat, an email for a free lesson, or a team request.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List each module or week with the one skill it teaches, in the order students meet them. Visitors deciding whether to enroll scan this list before anything else. Keep each line short and name real exercises, not topics.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a short instructor section with who you have taught and one result a past student got. Quote real students with their permission, and place one quote next to the enroll button, where the decision is made.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask only what the next step needs
fields.howto_step_5_des: Keep the form to fields you will use. A cohort needs a name and an email; a free lesson needs only the email; a team request needs a seat count and a work email. Add a placement question only when it changes the class a student joins.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Describe the page and each rule it follows, such as a 30-seat cap or an email for teams of 10 or more. Emergent builds the page and the enrollment table from that prompt. Change the cap or a question later with another prompt.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send a test enrollment down every path: a cohort seat, a free lesson, a placement score, and a team request. Check each saved row and every email it set off, then publish on your domain and share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is a course landing page?
faq_plan.a: A course landing page is a single page that sells one course and asks the visitor to take one step: enroll, claim a free lesson, or request seats for a team. It says who the course is for, what students can do by the end, and what each module covers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a course landing page?
faq_plan.a: Write the outcome the course delivers and pick its format, then list the syllabus by module. Then describe it to Emergent's AI landing page builder, which writes the page from your prompt and creates the database that stores each enrollment. Send a test enrollment through every path before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What do strong course landing page examples show above the fold?
faq_plan.a: A headline that names the result, a line naming the student it suits, and the enroll button with what it asks for: a price, an email, or a seat request. When you study course landing page examples, check whether the format sits beside that button as well, such as live for 6 weeks or self-paced.

faq_plan.q: Why do some online course landing page examples ask for an email instead of a sale?
faq_plan.a: They sell the course in two steps: a free lesson in exchange for an email first, then the paid course in the follow-up emails. Use that approach for a course a visitor is unlikely to buy on a first visit. Online course landing page examples built this way work like a lead generation landing page, where the signup is the goal.

faq_plan.q: Is a course landing page template enough to launch a course?
faq_plan.a: No. A course landing page template gives you the layout, but you still write the outcome and the syllabus, and enrollments still need somewhere to go. Emergent builds the layout and the place enrollments go from the same prompt, and every student is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What sections should an online course landing page have?
faq_plan.a: Give an online course landing page six sections: the headline with the outcome, who it is for, the syllabus by module, the instructor, student results, and the enroll form. Close with a short FAQ on the schedule and refunds, the questions people ask before they enroll.

faq_plan.q: Should ad traffic go to the course landing page or a separate page?
faq_plan.a: Send it to a separate page when the ad makes one narrow promise, such as a free first lesson for beginners. Build that ppc landing page around the ad's own wording and leave out the navigation, while the full course page keeps its menu for visitors who arrive from search. Save enrollments from both to the same table so you can compare them.

faq_plan.q: How long should a course landing page be?
faq_plan.a: Match the length to what you ask of the visitor. A free lesson needs a headline and an email field. A paid cohort needs the full syllabus, the instructor, student results, and answers about the schedule, since a visitor reads more before paying more.

faq_plan.q: How do I track enrollments from a course landing page?
faq_plan.a: Save each enrollment with the link that brought the visitor, then count enrollments by source and by cohort each week. Divide enrollments by page visits for the rate, and look at which source fills seats, not only which sends clicks. Pages Emergent builds can show those counts on a live dashboard that reads from a database you own.

faq_plan.q: When does a live workshop need its own page apart from the course landing page?
faq_plan.a: When it runs on one date and people can sign up for it alone. Give that session an event landing page with the date and the seats left near the top. Keep the workshop on the course page when it is part of the course price and every enrolled student attends.

plan.angle: The top 10 is design galleries (Dribbble, Pinterest, a Figma template), example roundups (Unbounce, Landingi, LearnWorlds) and how-to guides (Udemy, Kit, Kwiga); they show what a course page looks like but stop before a student enrolls. This page shows four course landing pages working by course format: a cohort course whose seat count drops with each enrollment, a self-paced course that trades its first lesson for an email, a language course that places each student with a short quiz, and a SQL course that sends team requests to the instructor. The FAQ answers what searchers ask about examples, templates, sections, length, ad traffic and tracking enrollments. Webinar, event, waitlist and sales pages are siblings and stay out of the headings.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Course Landing Page Shaped Around How You Teach'; hero 'Build a course landing page for a cohort, a self-paced course, or team training, with every enrollment in a database you own.' covers the whole job; how-to description is one sentence under 140 chars.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is example galleries and how-to guides; the page gives four worked examples by format (Cohort Course, Self-Paced Course, Placement Quiz, Team Training), a seven-step how-to and FAQ on examples, template, sections, length and tracking.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'Cap a cohort at the number you can teach', 'List each module or week with the one skill it teaches', 'a team request needs a seat count and a work email'.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on full sentences: 'Fernhollow Studio caps its 6-week watercolor cohort at 30 seats', 'Tell Emergent the course format and what to ask each student.'

craft.evidence: Short declaratives, one idea each: 'The count drops the moment an enrollment saves.' QC Q2/Q5/Q7 clean.

voice.evidence: Concrete unglamorous detail: 'Junie Calloway enrolled as student 24', 'Halvorsen Freight asked for 18 seats, and Bram got the email.' No hype verbs.

truth.evidence: why_table lists Landingi twice: columns 'Landingi / Leadpages / Instapage' and 'Landingi', with identical cells in every row. Emergent claims all map to claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, realtime, alerts, custom-domain, code-export, free-start); tab numbers agree (30 - 24 = 6; 4 of 6 in the 3-4 band; 18 >= 10).

distinct.evidence: Own stories by course format (seat cap, free lesson for an email, placement quiz, team-seat alert); sibling primaries only as FAQ link anchors (lead generation, ppc, event landing page).

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic written questions, all pass the PAA gate (pass 10, flag 0); answer-first ('No. A course landing page template gives you the layout...'); hub link in item 2, three sibling links; moat lines in items 5 and 9.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: '6 of 30' with 'Junie Calloway, Student 24'; '212 signups'; 'Odile Marchetti 4 of 6', '3 or 4 of 6: Intermediate'; 'Email to Bram Okafor, Team request: 18 seats, Rule 10 or more seats'.

findings.issue: The comparison table uses the grouped library entry 'Landingi / Leadpages / Instapage' and the single entry 'Landingi' side by side, so Landingi appears in two columns and every cell of the two columns is identical ('Templates and drag-and-drop, AI assist', 'Vendor lead storage and integrations', 'Tiered by traffic on most plans', 'Higher plans', 'Hosted only'). The reader sees a malformed table with one vendor compared against itself; HUB_RULES 5 asks for 3 distinct competitors that rank for the query. Only instance on the page (table.vs in the spec).
findings.fix: Regenerate with three distinct vendors, e.g. hubctl table <url> --vs Unbounce,Landingi,Leadpages --rows build,data,visitors,abtest,ownership (Unbounce and Landingi rank in the top 10), then QC to 0.
